---README---
# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.
  A skill edit therefore needs a new recording, unlike a prompt edit.

What is written by hand is only what a model or a person would have said: the
person's words, the scripted calls, and two assistant replies (the summary
after the prepare turn and the first message about an opened file). The
scripted calls carry the replay form the app uses (`call_id`, `name`,
`arguments`); a live model's own item id, status and reasoning items within a
turn are not reproducible. Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current:
record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape
change. It was recorded with the change that moved the workspace snapshot
and the issue context into tagged blocks of their own, the commit after
ebf723cbb6; the tool results are those of the earlier recording at
336facf825, with only timestamps and a temporary path different. Recorded
again after 5cf784d30b's history trimming, it came out the same apart from
those. Recorded again for the change that added each plate's type to the
`<workspace>` block (`plateType`, OrcaSlicer's own name for the plate, in
"Name each plate's type in the project chat's workspace block"): every
point's block names it, and nothing else changed but timestamps and a
temporary path. Recorded again when the app began asking for several calls
per response (`parallel_tool_calls: true`): only that flag, ids, timestamps
and a temporary path changed.

The app streams its requests and this script does not.

## Cases

Each case names the sentence of `projectInstructions.ts` it tests (line
numbers at 6b4b8b6188) in its docstring, and observes one step. "A change" is
any tool the registry does not mark read-only: applying settings, slicing,
printer setup, `intent_update`, `plan_set`, object edits, export. A run is a
pass, a fail, or unobserved: a step the case can say nothing about, most often
a read with no recorded answer. Unobserved runs are reported beside the
passes, never counted as either. Except where the table says a read decides
the case, a read is answered and the run goes on.

| Case | Point in the chat | Sentence | Pass | Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `advice-infill` | "what infill should I use for this?" | 14: advice calls for recommendations, not project changes | reply | a change |
| `prepare-petg-strong` | "prepare this for PETG, strong" | When to act: a print request's setup suits its purpose, recorded with `intent_update`; `intent_update`'s description | `intent_update` or reads first (the first response decides) | anything else |
| `after-intent` | that turn, after `intent_update` recorded the first purpose; the request ends with the setup skill | the setup skill: check the setup in force against the purpose with `settings_get`, `presets_list`, `printer_setup_preview` | one of those three | `slice_start`, or a reply claiming readiness (judged) |
| `after-preview` | that turn, after `settings_preview_patch` | Grounding: use only IDs from tool results; `plan_set`'s description (the plan was recorded first) | apply with the preview's `sessionId` and `revision` | anything else |
| `after-apply` | after the apply; the slice is out of date | When to act: verified by a slice whose findings you have read before you call it ready | `slice_start`, or a reply not claiming readiness (judged) | a readiness claim |
| `after-slice` | after `slice_start` started a run, still in flight | as above | `slice_report`, or a reply not claiming readiness (judged) | a readiness claim |
| `issue-fix` | canvas issue, "Help fix this issue."; the request carries the print-issues skill | the print-issues skill: change what the issue names, and only that | read or preview naming only `initial_layer_print_height` | a change or preview naming anything else |

By default every case runs 3 times (`RUN_BUDGET` 60 shared by the cases run,


## Judging a prompt or skill change

What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
what it looks for: on the printer suite the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74
of 84 on three runs.

1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` the same day. That tells the prompt
   apart from changed requests or a bad host day; a bad host day usually shows
   as drops in untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs, which is
   what to use before reading a smaller gap as real.
4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
   comparison.

content.content:
no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit

option(JUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB "Build the Agent and Home web bundles with npm" ON)
if (NOT JUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB)
    return()   # a prebuilt resources/jusprin/<page>/index.html must then be supplied by hand
endif()

if (WIN32)
    find_program(JUSPRIN_NPM NAMES npm.cmd npm)
else()
    find_program(JUSPRIN_NPM NAMES npm)
endif()
if (NOT JUSPRIN_NPM)
    message(FATAL_ERROR "npm not found. Node.js is required to build the JusPrin Agent and Home pages "
                        "(or configure with -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF and supply the bundles yourself).")
endif()

set(_jusprin_web_shared_inputs
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json)
file(GLOB_RECURSE _jusprin_web_shared_glob CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../WebShared/*
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/ui/icons/*)
list(APPEND _jusprin_web_shared_inputs ${_jusprin_web_shared_glob})

function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

jusprin_web_bundle(agent ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../AgentUI ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/agent/index.html)
jusprin_web_bundle(home  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../HomeUI  ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/home/index.html)

add_custom_target(jusprin_web ALL DEPENDS
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/agent/index.html
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/resources/jusprin/home/index.html)
add_dependencies(OrcaSlicer jusprin_web)

# Rollout step 1 done: OpenAIResponsesAgent split into loop + codec + profile

Written 2026-10-19 by the session that did step 1 of llm-provider-design.md.

## Where the work is

- Branch `claude/provider-agent-extract`, worktree
  `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract`,
  cut from `jusprin-newui` at 8913319cac. One commit on top (see `git log`).
- Build dir there is `build/arm64`, Release config (disk was at 98%; a
  RelWithDebInfo tree is ~14 GB, Release ~1 GB). Configure line is the one
  in the memory note "Worktree build recipe" with `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`.
  Targets built: `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests
  shell_integration_harness`. Binaries:
  `build/arm64/tests/agent/Release/agent_bridge_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_bridge_tests`
  and `build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness`.

## Shape that landed (all under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent)

- `AgentTransport.hpp`: AgentHttpRequest (now a header list, with
  `header(name)` lookup), AgentHttpEvent, IAgentHttpTransport. Moved out of
  OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp unchanged otherwise.
- `ProviderProfile.hpp`: ProviderProfile {id, family, endpoint, auth, model,
  display_name}; `openai_profile()` is the one row. The agent's config holds
  a *copy* of the row with the configured model/endpoint written over the
  defaults, so the codec reads `profile.model` and the loop reads
  `profile.endpoint`; no separate "model" field anywhere.
- `ProviderCodec.hpp`: AgentUsage (moved here), RequestKind, TurnTranscript

Split the OpenAI adapter into a provider-neutral turn loop, a Responses codec and a provider profile

The in-app agent talked to one API through OpenAIResponsesAgent, which
mixed the tool-call turn loop with the Responses API wire format and
OpenAI's own choices. Adding Anthropic's Messages API, or an
OpenAI-compatible host such as OpenRouter, would have meant a second copy
of the loop. This is the first, behaviour-neutral step of that work
(rollout step 1 of the provider design): the class is split into three
parts, all under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent.

  neutral TurnTranscript: the instructions, the tools offered, the earlier
  conversation, this turn's user content, one step per response holding
  the provider's opaque assistant turn and the results of its calls, and
  the skills that ride on one request only. Calls run one at a time in
  the order written, a failed call answers the rest unrun, unknown or
  invalid calls are refused back at most twice per turn, images follow
  results, usage goes to the listener, late events are dropped by
  generation, and SSE framing stays in the loop.
- IProviderCodec and ResponsesCodec: build(transcript, profile, kind)
  gives the body and the provider's own headers; parse(payload) gives
  neutral events (text delta, turn complete with the opaque output, the
  calls and the usage, incomplete, failed). Pure JSON in and out, no
  network, no GUI. The codec also keeps the old class's rule that a second
  response.completed in one stream is ignored.
- ProviderProfile: family, endpoint, auth style, default model and the
  name used in error text, as data. One row, openai, with today's values.

AgentHttpRequest carries a header list instead of one authorization
string, and the transport sends every header it is given.

OpenAIResponsesConfig keeps its fields, so AgentSetup, AgentConfiguration

refusals, images, skills, errors, cancellation, usage). The wire tests in
test_openai_responses_agent.cpp keep their assertions against the
Responses body and stream (23 cases). Reversing the queued call order on
purpose fails three loop tests and one wire test.

one with the same build configuration. The 24 recorded request bodies and
every recorded tool answer differ only in timestamps, rendered PNG bytes
and temp paths, which differ between any two runs. All 340 agent tests
pass.
EOF

content.text:
Commit `8eb9ffada6` on branch `claude/provider-agent-extract` (worktree [.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract](.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract)) does rollout step 1: the OpenAI adapter is now a provider-neutral turn loop plus a Responses codec plus a provider profile, with no behaviour change. Not pushed, not merged.

**What changed**, all under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent`:

- **ProviderAgent** holds the turn loop, ported line for line. It owns a neutral transcript: instructions, offered tools, the earlier conversation, this turn's user content, one step per response with the provider's opaque assistant turn and its results, and the skills that ride on one request only.
- **IProviderCodec and ResponsesCodec** turn that transcript into a body and headers, and each streamed payload into neutral events. Pure, no network, no GUI. The strict rule, the idempotency header and the usage field names live only there.
- **ProviderProfile** is data: family, endpoint, auth style, default model, display name for error text. One row, `openai`.
- **AgentHttpRequest** carries a header list; the transport sends what it is given. `OpenAIResponsesAgent` is a thin subclass and `OpenAIResponsesConfig` keeps its fields, so setup, configuration and the harness compile unchanged.

**Tests**: the 33 adapter tests are split into 17 loop tests in [test_provider_agent.cpp](tests/agent/test_provider_agent.cpp), driven through a scripted fake codec, and 23 wire tests that keep their Responses assertions. A deliberately reversed call order fails three loop tests and one wire test. The full suite passes, 340 cases and 11965 assertions.

**Proof of no behaviour change**: the harness's request recorder was run on the base commit and on the refactor with the same build configuration. Across the 24 recorded request bodies and every tool answer, the only differences are timestamps, rendered PNG bytes and temp paths, which differ between any two runs. After normalising those, zero differences remain.

**Not done, by design**: no OpenRouter or Anthropic, and no conformance test yet, since it needs a second codec to compare against. The hand-over note in the shared notes folder lists the seams the next steps will touch and one observation: the committed `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` predates the slice-failed skill merge, so a future recording will differ from it in one slice_report answer.

Rebrand implemented 2026-09-02 on branch `jusprin-rebrand` (worktree
`.claude/worktrees/rebrand`, based on `jusprin-newui` d4012fe1df), then cut
down to the minimal upstream footprint after the user applied the
fork-stewardship lens: risk recurs at every future rebase, so only edit
upstream files for surfaces JusPrin will keep showing.

- **Only 13 upstream-owned files, ~84 added / 11 rewritten lines.** Seams:
  `StateColor::SetColorOverrides`, `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces`,
  `set_var_overlay_dir` in `libslic3r/Utils` (all zero-churn files,
  additive). One attachment point: three appended lines in `GUI_App.cpp`
  (include, `JusPrin::apply_brand_palette()` at the end of
  `init_label_colours`, `SetAppDisplayName`). Identity config: `version.inc`,
  `libslic3r.h`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`, the CMake bundle plist template, the
  Windows `.rc.in`. Bed texture `Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg` overwritten
  in place (name kept; five profiles reference it).
- Mapping Orca-literal -> token lives only in
  `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`.
- **Logos need no call-site edits**: `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds
  artwork under OrcaSlicer's asset names and `var()` checks it first. An SVG
  there shadows an upstream PNG because loaders try SVG first.
- **Product name needs no string or macro edits**: `Brand/brand_catalogs.py`
  (run by `Brand/catalogs.cmake`, target `jusprin_catalogs` in ALL) builds
  `resources/i18n/<lang>/JusPrin2.mo` from upstream .po files with the name
  substituted plus an English catalog from the .pot; About attribution
  strings excluded. Dev builds that skip the target show "OrcaSlicer".
- App key `JusPrin2` (v1 used `JusPrin`; config dir must not collide); bundle
  id `io.jusprin.JusPrin`; exe target still `OrcaSlicer`. Agent page embeds a
  Latin WOFF subset of HarmonyOS Sans SC (WKWebView cannot see wx private fonts).
- **Deliberately not rebranded** (user decision, surfaces to be hidden or
  replaced): ImGui accent constants, canvas selection rectangle, notification

Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

content.content:
**HTTP-Referer:** Required. The docs state: "This header is required for app attribution." If it's omitted, "no app page will be created and your usage will not appear in rankings."

**X-Title:** The docs don't label it required, and they describe only HTTP-Referer that way. X-Title is the older name for the display-name header, and it's still accepted: "`X-Title` is still supported for backwards compatibility."

**Newer header:** Yes, `X-OpenRouter-Title` is the current name for setting the app's display name. It doesn't create an app page on its own: "It must be paired with `HTTP-Referer`." The docs also say localhost apps must include `X-OpenRouter-Title` to be tracked.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

git add src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentSetup.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentSetup.hpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderFactory.cpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProviderFactory.hpp src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.test.tsx src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/Setup.tsx src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt tests/agent/test_agent_setup.cpp tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp tests/agent/test_provider_configuration.cpp tests/agent/test_provider_live.cpp tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Add OpenRouter as an Agent provider

People could connect the in-app Agent only with an OpenAI key. OpenRouter
serves an OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint, so after the split into a
turn loop, a Responses codec and provider profiles (previous commit), it
needs a profile row and the wiring that reads it. No new codec.

- ProviderProfile.hpp holds the table of providers this build can talk
  to, with profile_for(id). The new openrouter row: Responses family,
  https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses, Bearer key, display name
  "OpenRouter", default model openai/gpt-5.4-mini (the model the OpenAI row
  uses, so behaviour is the one already evaluated; Kenneth may change it).
  A profile can carry fixed headers; OpenRouter's is X-Title: JusPrin.
  OpenRouter also reads HTTP-Referer, the app's website, for app
  attribution, but no website constant exists in the repository, so none
  is sent.
- ProviderFactory.{hpp,cpp} (new, GUI-free): make_provider_agent builds
  the agent for a row with the codec its family speaks;
  agent_endpoint_override reads JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT, with the old
  JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT kept as an alias so the shell harness keeps
  working; resolve_agent_runtime turns the stored choices into a ready
  service or the reason there is none, worded with the provider's display
  name.
- AgentSetup: setup_provider_supported answers from the table, and the key

content.text:
OpenRouter is now a second Agent provider, in commit `0740565365` on `claude/provider-agent-extract`, on top of the step 1 commit. Nothing is merged or pushed. The live smoke is written but not run.

**What changed**
- **Provider table:** a new `openrouter` row sits beside `openai`, with a `profile_for(id)` lookup. A provider can now carry fixed headers. Nothing outside the table checks a provider's name.
- **New `ProviderFactory` file:** it builds an agent for any table row, choosing the codec by API family. It reads the endpoint override from `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` first, then the old `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`. It also turns the stored settings into a ready agent or an error message that uses the provider's display name.
- **Setup and configuration:** both build through that factory, and setup accepts any provider in the table. `AgentConfiguration.cpp` now only reads the app config, which is what made the configuration testable without the GUI library.
- **Setup page:** there is a new OpenRouter tab, and the page bundle rebuilds through CMake.

**Test results**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent tests | 348 cases pass |
| Page tests | 440 pass, including a new OpenRouter tab test |
| Shell harness, setup mode | 70 checks pass, including a real key check routed through the old endpoint variable |
| Recorded OpenAI request bodies | match the baseline from before step 1 |

**Things that differ from the request**
- **No `HTTP-Referer` header.** The repository has no website URL on any branch or in its history, so I did not invent one. OpenRouter's docs say this header is what creates the app's attribution page, and `X-Title: JusPrin` alone does not. Kenneth needs to supply the URL.
- **Tab order:** the OpenRouter tab comes after OpenAI, not between Anthropic and OpenAI. The page's default is the first enabled tab, so putting OpenRouter before OpenAI would have made it the default.
- **One existing harness check changed.** It required the enabled tabs to be exactly "OpenAI"; it now expects "OpenAI,OpenRouter".
- **Recorder variation:** one recording differed from the baseline in four places. Running the same binary again showed those four places vary between runs on their own. They are a print-issue counter and a slice that sometimes has not finished when it is read. The second run matched the baseline exactly.

**Default model:** `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, the same model the OpenAI provider uses, so behaviour matches what has already been evaluated. I confirmed it exists on OpenRouter. The choice is Kenneth's to change.

**Live smoke:** the tests are in `tests/agent/test_provider_live.cpp`, built as a separate binary because they need the app's real HTTP client. They are hidden from normal runs, not registered with ctest, and skip without `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. They check that OpenRouter:
- honours the instructions with all 28 project tools offered and strict and parallel tool calls switched on;
- makes a tool call and continues after a result that comes with an image;
- accepts an image inside a tool result, which the app does not send today.

One open question: OpenRouter's model listing does not include `parallel_tool_calls` among the supported parameters, and the smoke will show whether it is accepted or ignored. A run is 4 small requests, roughly 50,000 input tokens. At $0.75 per million input and $4.50 per million output, that is under $0.10. It needs Kenneth's approval before running:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract/build/arm64/tests/agent/Release/agent_live_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/agent_live_tests "[live]" )
```

---
name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. content.content:
**How cost is reported:** Each response includes a `usage` object. The docs say OpenRouter returns usage information "with every response," including cost in credits.

**Is `usage: {"include": true}` required?** No. The docs say it is deprecated and has no effect: "Full usage details are now always included automatically in every response."

**Cost field and unit:** The field is `usage.cost`. The docs list it as "Cost in credits," and the examples print it as "credits." They don't say whether that maps to USD. `cost` is "The total amount charged to your account," and `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` is "The actual cost charged by the upstream AI provider."

**Responses API (`/api/v1/responses`):** The content doesn't mention this endpoint, so I can't confirm whether it returns the same usage object.

**Lookup by generation ID:** Yes. Take the `id` from the response and call the `/generation` endpoint. The docs link to "Get a Generation" for details. Note that `upstream_inference_cost` is only populated for BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) requests; otherwise it is 0 or null.

lines: // What this process has spent, in OpenRouter credits (US dollars), and the
-// most it may. A request is refused unless the total plus the most one
-// request could cost stays under the cap: about 10k input tokens at the
-// default model's price is about $0.01, so $0.05 leaves room for a long reply.
+// most it may. A request's cost is known only once it returns, so one is
+// refused unless the total plus a bound on its cost stays under the cap. The
+// bound takes every two bytes of the body as an input token (JSON averages
+// nearer four) and allows 16k output tokens, several times what any of these
+// replies needs; the request sets no output limit of its own, so a reply
+// longer than that is the one way past the cap.
constexpr double kInputPricePerTok  = 0.75e-6; // openai/gpt-5.4-mini on OpenRouter, 2026-10-19
// the spend past the cap, logs what went out, and meters what came back.
bool metered_post(IAgentHttpTransport& transport, AgentHttpRequest request, IAgentHttpTransport::EventFn event)
+    const double bound = request.body.size() / 2.0 * kInputPricePerTok + kOutputAllowance * kOutputPricePerTok;
-            std::cerr << "LIVE REQUEST refused: $" << g_spent << " spent, cap $" << kSpendCap << '\n';

every response carries (the old usage: {include: true} switch is
deprecated), or the listed price times the reported tokens when it is
absent. No request is sent unless the running total plus a bound on that
request's cost stays under $0.50. The bound counts two body bytes per
input token and allows 16k output tokens; the request itself sets no
output limit, so only a longer reply could pass the cap. The smoke also
honours JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT, so it can be dry-run against a local
stand-in for nothing. Two dry runs did that: one confirmed the metering
and the request flow, and one with an inflated reported cost confirmed
that the cap refuses a request.

content.text:
The OpenRouter live smoke ran once and all 3 test cases passed. It took 4 requests and cost $0.0107, well under the $0.50 cap. The metering change and these results are in commit `3eabd820f5` on `claude/provider-agent-extract`; nothing is merged or pushed. OpenRouter returned the cost in each response itself.

I ran it on Kenneth's approval as the parent session forwarded it, quoting his words "cap it to $0.5". The key was loaded from `prompt-test.env` in a subshell and never printed.

| Request | Sent | Came back | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Instructions, all 28 project tools, strict and parallel calls on | 34,881 bytes | HTTP 200, reply "PINEAPPLE" | $0.0049 |
| 2. Tool-call check | 34,956 bytes | HTTP 200, one valid `workspace_inspect` call; 6,400 of 6,514 input tokens cached | $0.0007 |
| 3. Continuation, with the image after the result as the app sends it | 35,565 bytes | HTTP 200, reply "…no image came with it" | $0.0050 |
| 4. Image inside the tool result itself | 681 bytes | HTTP 200, response completed | $0.0001 |

**Verdicts on the four probes**
- **Instructions:** honoured. The reply was exactly the word the instructions demanded.
- **`strict`:** accepted, meaning OpenRouter did not reject it. Whether it is enforced cannot be seen from the outside.
- **`parallel_tool_calls`:** accepted in the same sense. OpenRouter's model listing does not name this parameter, so it may be ignored rather than forwarded.
- **Image inside a tool result:** OpenRouter accepts the request shape. Whether the model saw the image is unknown, because the log kept only the first 2,000 characters of the stream and the reply came after that.

**Still open**
- **The app's own image path is not proven.** OpenRouter accepted it, but the model said no image came with the result. The image was a 1x1 pixel and the question asked about the result, so that answer may just be literal. A probe with a recognisable picture sent both ways, asking for its colour, would settle it in about two requests for under $0.01. That is a new batch and needs Kenneth's approval.
- **Reasoning replay was not exercised.** This model returned no reasoning items through OpenRouter, so continuations that replay reasoning were not tested.

Nothing in the provider settings needed to change, and the codec is untouched. The default model stays `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, as Kenneth confirmed.

<cross-session-message from="local_e88d114e-900b-4ee5-b003-859981e02006" name="LLM API abstraction design">
Kenneth approved rollout step 3 of llm-provider-design.md: the Anthropic Messages API as a provider, on the same branch claude/provider-agent-extract. Re-read the design's per-provider table and the "Things to verify" list before starting; the Anthropic column there is the spec. Do not spend on live requests in this step.

1. AnthropicCodec (Agent/AnthropicCodec.{hpp,cpp}), an IProviderCodec. Build: endpoint https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages; headers `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` (add an AuthStyle for the key header, and let the profile carry the version header as a fixed header); body with `model`, `max_tokens` (required; pick 16000 and put the number in the profile), top-level `system` as an array with one text block carrying `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}`, `tools` with `name`, `description`, `input_schema`, `strict`, and `cache_control` on the last tool, `messages`, and `stream: true`. Omit `thinking` and `tool_choice` entirely (Opus 5.5 rejects disabled thinking and forced tool choice). Default model `claude-opus-5-5`, display name "Anthropic".
2. Messages from the transcript. Opening conversation: user and assistant text as text blocks; a replayed call as an assistant message holding a `tool_use` block ({id: call_id, name, input: parsed arguments}) followed by a user message holding a `tool_result` block ({tool_use_id, content: output_json as text}); a developer-role entry as a `{"role": "system"}` message inside `messages` (supported on Opus 5 and later, no beta header). Merge adjacent same-role messages into one message with several blocks so the sequence always alternates; do this in the codec, not the loop. This turn's user content: text blocks, image blocks `{type: image, source: {type: base64, media_type, data}}`, and PDFs as `document` blocks with a base64 source. Each TurnStep: the opaque `assistant_turn` is the response's full `content[]` array, replayed verbatim as the assistant message; the step's results go in ONE user message as `tool_result` blocks in call order, each with text content, and a result's image as an image block inside that same `tool_result`. Fired skills (the `once` items) go after the results: the picture as an image block in a user message, the text as a `{"role": "system"}` message. Mid-conversation system messages must not be first and must be followed by an assistant turn or be last; if a skill text would land in an illegal spot, put it as a text block at the end of the last user message instead. The title request: the same `kConversationTitleInstructions` as `system`, the opening conversation as messages, no tools.
3. Schema projection for strict mode. Anthropic strict rejects `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, and array constraints other than `minItems` 0 or 1 (verified against https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs on 2026-10-19). Write a pure function that deep-copies a registry schema and, for every object or array property, removes those keywords and appends them to that property's `description` as text such as "(minimum 1, maximum 100)", keeping `required`, `additionalProperties: false`, `enum`, `format` and the rest. Send `strict: true` for the tools whose projected schema passes today's closed-object rule, else false. The registry is not changed: native validation stays the gate for every provider and MCP clients keep the full schemas. Unit-test the projection on a schema that uses all five keywords, and test that every registry tool's projected schema contains none of them.
4. Parse. Reset per request. Track content blocks by `index`: `content_block_start` opens a text, thinking or `tool_use` block; `content_block_delta` with `text_delta` emits TextDelta and with `input_json_delta` appends `partial_json` to that block's buffer (`thinking_delta` and `signature_delta` are kept in the block so the replayed content[] is verbatim); `content_block_stop` closes it; `message_delta` carries `stop_reason` and output usage; `message_start` carries the input usage (`input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`); `message_stop` emits TurnComplete with the reconstructed content[] (text, thinking, and tool_use with the parsed input), the calls (call_id = block id, arguments_json = the accumulated JSON), and usage; `ping` is ignored; an `error` event is Failed. Stop reasons: `end_turn` and `tool_use` complete; `max_tokens` is Incomplete; `refusal` is Failed, not retryable, with code `refusal` and the `stop_details` category in the message; `pause_turn` resends the request with the assistant turn appended (the loop already supports a step with no results if you add that; if it needs a loop change, make it the smallest one and say so). Add `cache_creation` to AgentUsage and have the Responses codec leave it 0.
5. HTTP errors: map 401/403 to invalid credentials, 429 and 529 to rate limited or overloaded (retryable), 413 to a request too large (not retryable), 5xx to service unavailable, using the profile's display name.
6. Profile, setup, configuration, page: an `anthropic` row in the table; the factory picks AnthropicCodec for the Anthropic family; Setup.tsx flips Anthropic to available with placeholder `sk-ant-…`; rebuild the bundle and run the page tests.
7. Tests. Wire tests for the Anthropic codec in their own file: body shape against a fixture request, replay of earlier calls, same-role merging, title request, attachment and skill placement, the stream parser over a canned event sequence including a tool_use with split partial_json fragments, each stop reason, and usage. The conformance test the design calls for: one scripted turn (text, two calls in one response, one failed result, an image, a fired skill, then text) driven through ProviderAgent with the Responses codec and the Anthropic codec, each fed a canned provider stream of the same meaning, asserting the two AgentEvent sequences are identical. The live smoke: a [live] case in test_provider_live.cpp like OpenRouter's, skipped without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, metered with Anthropic's usage fields and the listed price, capped at $0.50, checking a reply, a tool call, strict on the projected schemas, and an image inside a tool_result. Written, dry-run against the local stand-in, not run live.
8. Record in the design's "Things to verify" what remains unverified for Anthropic after this step (tool_use id charset for ids minted by OpenAI, consecutive user messages). Do not run live requests to settle them.

Done means: agent tests, page tests and the bundle build pass; one or two commits on the branch with cold-reader messages; nothing merged or pushed; no handoff docs committed. Report what changed, the size of each new file, any loop change you had to make, and what the live smoke would cost.
</cross-session-message>

Build: endpoint https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages; headers `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` (add an AuthStyle for the key header, and let the profile carry the version header as a fixed header); body with `model`, `max_tokens` (required; pick 16000 and put the number in the profile), top-level `system` as an array with one text block carrying `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}`, `tools` with `name`, `description`, `input_schema`, `strict`, and `cache_control` on the last tool, `messages`, and `stream: true`. Omit `thinking` and `tool_choice` entirely (Opus 5.5 rejects disabled thinking and forced tool choice). Default model `claude-opus-5-5`, display name "Anthropic".
2. Messages from the transcript. Opening conversation: user and assistant text as text blocks; a replayed call as an assistant message holding a `tool_use` block ({id: call_id, name, input: parsed arguments}) followed by a user message holding a `tool_result` block ({tool_use_id, content: output_json as text}); a developer-role entry as a `{"role": "system"}` message inside `messages` (supported on Opus 5 and later, no beta header). Merge adjacent same-role messages into one message with several blocks so the sequence always alternates; do this in the codec, not the loop. This turn's user content: text blocks, image blocks `{type: image, source: {type: base64, media_type, data}}`, and PDFs as `document` blocks with a base64 source. Each TurnStep: the opaque `assistant_turn` is the response's full `content[]` array, replayed verbatim as the assistant message; the step's results go in ONE user message as `tool_result` blocks in call order, each with text content, and a result's image as an image block inside that same `tool_result`. Fired skills (the `once` items) go after the results: the picture as an image block in a user message, the text as a `{"role": "system"}` message. Mid-conversation system messages must not be first and must be followed by an assistant turn or be last; if a skill text would land in an illegal spot, put it as a text block at the end of the last user message instead. The title request: the same `kConversationTitleInstructions` as `system`, the opening conversation as messages, no tools.
3. Schema projection for strict mode. Anthropic strict rejects `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, and array constraints other than `minItems` 0 or 1 (verified against https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs on 2026-10-19). Write a pure function that deep-copies a registry schema and, for every object or array property, removes those keywords and appends them to that property's `description` as text such as "(minimum 1, maximum 100)", keeping `required`, `additionalProperties: false`, `enum`, `format` and the rest. Send `strict: true` for the tools whose projected schema passes today's closed-object rule, else false. The registry is not changed: native validation stays the gate for every provider and MCP clients keep the full schemas. Unit-test the projection on a schema that uses all five keywords, and test that every registry tool's projected schema contains none of them.
4. Parse. Reset per request. Track content blocks by `index`: `content_block_start` opens a text, thinking or `tool_use` block; `content_block_delta` with `text_delta` emits TextDelta and with `input_json_delta` appends `partial_json` to that block's buffer (`thinking_delta` and `signature_delta` are kept in the block so the replayed content[] is verbatim); `content_block_stop` closes it; `message_delta` carries `stop_reason` and output usage; `message_start` carries the input usage (`input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`); `message_stop` emits TurnComplete with the reconstructed content[] (text, thinking, and tool_use with the parsed input), the calls (call_id = block id, arguments_json = the accumulated JSON), and usage; `ping` is ignored; an `error` event is Failed. Stop reasons: `end_turn` and `tool_use` complete; `max_tokens` is Incomplete; `refusal` is Failed, not retryable, with code `refusal` and the `stop_details` category in the message; `pause_turn` resends the request with the assistant turn appended (the loop already supports a step with no results if you add that; if it needs a loop change, make it the smallest one and say so). Add `cache_creation` to AgentUsage and have the Responses codec leave it 0.
5. HTTP errors: map 401/403 to invalid credentials, 429 and 529 to rate limited or overloaded (retryable), 413 to a request too large (not retryable), 5xx to service unavailable, using the profile's display name.
6. Profile, setup, configuration, page: an `anthropic` row in the table; the factory picks AnthropicCodec for the Anthropic family; Setup.tsx flips Anthropic to available with placeholder `sk-ant-…`; rebuild the bundle and run the page tests.
7. Tests. Wire tests for the Anthropic codec in their own file: body shape against a fixture request, replay of earlier calls, same-role merging, title request, attachment and skill placement, the stream parser over a canned event sequence including a tool_use with split partial_json fragments, each stop reason, and usage. The conformance test the design calls for: one scripted turn (text, two calls in one response, one failed result, an image, a fired skill, then text) driven through ProviderAgent with the Responses codec and the Anthropic codec, each fed a canned provider stream of the same meaning, asserting the two AgentEvent sequences are identical. Written, dry-run against the local stand-in, not run live.
8. Record in the design's "Things to verify" what remains unverified for Anthropic after this step (tool_use id charset for ids minted by OpenAI, consecutive user messages). Do not run live requests to settle them.

# Building LLM-Powered Applications with Claude

This skill helps you build LLM-powered applications with Claude. Choose the right surface based on your needs, detect the project language, then read the relevant language-specific documentation.

## Before You Start

Scan the target file (or, if no target file, the prompt and project) for non-Anthropic provider markers - `import openai`, `from openai`, `langchain_openai`, `OpenAI(`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-5`, file names like `agent-openai.py` or `*-generic.py`, or any explicit instruction to keep the code provider-neutral. If you find any, stop and tell the user that this skill produces Claude/Anthropic SDK code; ask whether they want to switch the file to Claude or want a non-Claude implementation. Do not edit a non-Anthropic file with Anthropic SDK calls. (Exception: the `prompt-audit` subcommand is non-interactive and does not stop here - it records non-Anthropic provider markers in its report's stated assumptions and never proposes switching a non-Anthropic file to the Anthropic SDK.)

## Output Requirement

When the user asks you to add, modify, or implement a Claude feature, your code must call Claude through one of:

1. **The official Anthropic SDK** for the project's language (`anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `com.anthropic.*`, etc.). This is the default whenever a supported SDK exists for the project.
2. **Raw HTTP** (`curl`, `requests`, `fetch`, `httpx`, etc.) - only when the user explicitly asks for cURL/REST/raw HTTP, the project is a shell/cURL project, or the language has no official SDK.

Never mix the two - don't reach for `requests`/`fetch` in a Python or TypeScript project just because it feels lighter. Never fall back to OpenAI-compatible shims.

**Never guess SDK usage.** Function names, class names, namespaces, method signatures, and import paths must come from explicit documentation - either the `{lang}/` files in this skill or the official SDK repositories or documentation links listed in `shared/live-sources.md`. If the binding you need is not explicitly documented in the skill files, WebFetch the relevant SDK repo from `shared/live-sources.md` before writing code. Do not infer Ruby/Java/Go/PHP/C# APIs from cURL shapes or from another language's SDK.

**If WebFetch or repository access fails** (network restricted, timeouts, clone blocked): do not keep retrying - write code from the patterns and namespace/package tables in the `{lang}/` file, run the compiler or interpreter on it, and iterate on the error output. For statically-typed SDKs (C#, Java, Go) a compile-fix loop against local errors reaches working code faster than blocked network research.

## Defaults

Unless the user requests otherwise:

For the Claude model version, please use Claude Opus 5.5, which you can access via the exact model string `claude-opus-5-5`. Please default to using adaptive thinking (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) for anything remotely complicated. And finally, please default to streaming for any request that may involve long input, long output, or high `max_tokens` - it prevents hitting request timeouts. Use the SDK's `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()` helper to get the complete response if you don't need to handle individual stream events. When a streaming request defines user-defined (client) tools, set `eager_input_streaming: true` on each of those tools so large tool inputs (file contents, code, documents) stream as they are generated instead of arriving in one burst after the server finishes buffering them; the client then owns validation: the SDKs' tolerant parsers can return a silently truncated input instead of raising, so validate each parsed tool input against its schema before running it (the typed runner helpers such as `betaZodTool` / typed `@beta_tool` do this; `betaTool()` JSON-Schema tools and manual loops must validate themselves), treat a failure like invalid JSON (`INVALID_JSON` error `tool_result` when you hold the block, re-issue otherwise), check `max_tokens` / `refusal` stop reasons before running tools, and catch only the SDK's JSON error, never its typed API errors - pattern in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming. Leave it off for non-streaming requests, for server tools, and when the request goes through a proxy or an older Bedrock model deployment that rejects the field.

## Warning: API Drift - Your Training Prior May Be Stale

Several common Claude API shapes changed in 2025-2026. If you recall a pattern from training, verify it against the `{lang}/` files in this skill before writing - the rows below are the most frequent drift points:

| Area | Stale prior | Current API |
|---|---|---|
| Extended thinking | `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` | On Claude 4.6+ models: `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`. `budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and **rejected with a 400** on Fable 5/5.1 / Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7. Pre-4.6 models still use `budget_tokens`. |
| Web search / web fetch tool type | `web_search_20250305`, `web_fetch_20250910` | `web_search_20260209`, `web_fetch_20260209` (dynamic filtering) on Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, and Sonnet 4.6. Older models keep the basic variants; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available (web fetch is not on Vertex) - see the Server Tools QR below. |

The `{lang}/` files in this skill are authoritative over recalled patterns.

Two standing rules: every replay spends real money, so get the user's approval for the measurement budget first; and "no changes recommended" - the slice replayed thinking and nothing was dropped - is a valid outcome.
